title: The IMF Executive Board will consider Sri Lanka’s Article IV Consultation and seventh review under the Extended Fund Facility on 2 December 2026.
body_paragraphs: The session also covers requests for waivers of non‑observance and a financing assurances review under the four‑year programme (EFF, a medium‑term arrangement that supports macroeconomic reforms). If approved, the discussion could unlock about US$345 million and keep cumulative disbursements on track into early 2027.

The Government targets a primary surplus of 2.3% of GDP in 2027 while gross reserves stood near US$7 billion by end‑October. Foreign‑currency debt service resumes to commercial and bilateral creditors from 2027–2028 at close to US$6.6 billion across the two years, making continued multilateral engagement a key policy anchor.

title: The OPEC Fund approved a US$30 million policy‑based loan for Sri Lanka’s reform programme.
body_paragraphs: The facility comprises US$24 million from Ordinary Capital Resources and US$6 million from Special Capital Resources. It complements World Bank Development Policy financing under the “Reforms for Growth, Resilience and Openness” operation.
Cabinet cleared the borrowing proposal submitted by the Finance Minister. The funding supports macroeconomic stabilisation, fiscal sustainability measures and steps to open the economy to investment.
bold_phrases: Reforms for Growth, Resilience and Openness

title: Access Engineering won three expressway packages worth Rs. 68 billion for the Central and Ruwanpura projects.
body_paragraphs: Letters of acceptance dated 19 November covered Package 1J of Central Expressway Section 4 and Packages 1E and 1G of Ruwanpura Phase 1. The combined awards equal about 13.7% of the Rs. 494.8 billion recently approved across 23 lots.
The new wins exceed the company’s end‑June order book and follow a Rs. 18.7 billion Central Expressway package secured in May. Work on the Ruwanpura first phase is scheduled to begin on 1 December.

title: Colombo Port handled 791,811 TEUs in October, putting a new annual throughput record within reach a month early.
body_paragraphs: Transshipment rose 10.0% year‑on‑year to 636,623 TEUs and accounted for 80.4% of total volume, while domestic laden imports fell 15.5% to 51,898 TEUs. Colombo West International Terminal grew 46.6% to 175,180 TEUs and delivered the port’s entire net gain for the month.
For the first ten months, cumulative throughput reached 7.52 million TEUs, up 8.6% from a year earlier. The port now needs 772,561 TEUs to surpass the 2025 record of 8.29 million TEUs.

title: Sri Lanka’s Defence Secretary joined the Colombo Security Conclave National Security Advisers’ meeting in Malé on 25 November.
body_paragraphs: The discussions focused on maritime safety, counter‑terrorism, transnational crime, cyber security and disaster relief, the five pillars of the platform. Sri Lanka highlighted its “Ratama Ekata” drug‑control mission and the need to protect submarine cables through coordinated domain awareness.

title: The marine regulator moved to seek compensation over a diesel spill that polluted the Muthuwella coastline.
body_paragraphs: The Marine Environment Protection Authority said the leak originated at Jaya Container Terminal tank No. 108 on 21 November, with about 95% of inflow to the sea contained by 23 November. Investigations under the Marine Pollution Prevention Act will determine liability before legal action.

title: Trade unions marked a National Day of Protest against the 2027 Budget on 23 November.
body_paragraphs: Public‑sector groups across health, education, management services and technical cadres mobilised around a demand for a Rs. 25,000 interim allowance. Doctor, teacher and principal unions also signalled readiness for escalated action if grievances remain unresolved.

title: Tea production fell to 192.62 Mn/Kgs in January–September 2026, down 6.54 Mn/Kgs from a year earlier.
body_paragraphs: Exports declined 8.91 Mn/Kgs to 189.41 Mn/Kgs while the rupee‑term national sale average edged up by Rs. 9.64 to Rs. 1,170.20 per kilogramme. Türkiye became the top buyer at 35.71 Mn/Kgs, more than doubling year‑on‑year, as Libya and Iraq contracted.

title: SriLankan Airlines lost share in key markets in October as new nonstop rivals entered UK and Australia routes.
body_paragraphs: The UK share slipped to 38.87% while British Airways operated eight days of its winter Gatwick–Colombo service, and Australia fell to 38.44% as Jetstar reached 19.03%. In France, new long‑haul low‑cost capacity is set to add further pressure in December.

title: The Asian Development Bank approved a US$200 million package to ease credit constraints for small firms.
body_paragraphs: The programme combines US$100 million in investment lines channelled via participating lenders with a US$100 million policy‑based loan to strengthen credit reporting, expand guarantees and curb predatory digital lending. At least one in five climate‑related beneficiaries will be owned or led by women.

title: Sri Lanka welcomed its two‑millionth visitor of 2026 on 20 November, reaching the mark for a third straight year.
body_paragraphs: The milestone came three days later than in 2025 as a March–April slump offset early gains, leaving January–November 18 arrivals 1.4% behind last year. Authorities now need roughly 8,740 entries a day through year‑end to surpass the 2025 tally of 2.36 million.
